A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same optimizer–group fairness study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including relocated material and v2's added checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original optimizer simulations, fairness and classification experiments on CelebA, FairFace and MS-COCO, significance tests, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds joint hyperparameter tuning, tabular fairness-intervention experiments, and optimizer-variant comparisons.

M1.justification: The analyzed SGD, RMSProp and Adam update rules, original vision architectures, and training losses remain unchanged. Additional existing optimizers and FairBatch are evaluated without introducing or revising a proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains all three vision datasets and adds gender-sensitive fairness evaluation on ProPublica COMPAS and AdultCensus (Table 4). This substantially extends the evaluated data domain to tabular applications.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained SGD, RMSProp and Adam comparisons, v2 evaluates AdamW, AdaBound and SGD with momentum in Appendix N/Table 6. Table 4 also introduces comparisons with and without FairBatch, identified by reference 47.

E3.justification: Alongside the retained learning-rate-only tuning protocol, v2 adds joint Bayesian tuning of learning rate, decay rate and batch size on CelebA/ViT (Table 1). The new tabular experiment introduces with/without-intervention controls and lower-is-better fairness-gap metrics (Table 4); the original vision ratio metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds checks of whether fairness advantages survive joint hyperparameter tuning, whether optimizer variants support the second-moment-normalization explanation, and whether benefits complement FairBatch. The original imbalance experiment and simulation sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 specifies ten-run averages for the added tabular experiment. The existing two-run benchmark averages, ten-run Wilcoxon tests, five-run downsampling experiment and 1,000-run simulations remain unchanged. No new uncertainty-estimation method or increase in runs for existing experiments is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 4 and 6 add substantial result sets while previously reported results remain unchanged. For example, Table 6 reports gender FEOD of 64.90, 61.10 and 61.12 for AdamW, AdaBound and SGD with momentum. Table 4 reports COMPAS demographic-parity gaps with FairBatch of 0.86, 0.86 and 2.60 for Adam, RMSProp and SGD.

T1.justification: Appendices G and I add Theorems 4 and 5 and proof arguments extending the update-disparity and single-step demographic-parity bounds from isotropic to anisotropic Gaussian gradient noise. The original theorems remain; Theorem 3's existing proof is relocated to Appendix H.

C1.justification: The principal scientific claims in the abstract, introduction and conclusion remain stable. v2 adds source-code release to the abstract and explicitly lists public code availability as a fourth contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the tabular results as evidence of applicability beyond vision and complementarity with fairness interventions. Appendix N explains the optimizer-variant findings through second-moment normalization and its restriction in AdaBound. The original imbalance interpretation and qualification against universal fairness guarantees remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a public source-code link and states that a README provides reproduction instructions. Existing hardware, preprocessing, training-budget and hyperparameter disclosures are retained. Detailed search ranges for the new joint tuning and implementation details for the tabular experiments are not supplied.

R1.justification: Related work adds connections to implicit fairness in unconstrained learning and fairness surrogate functions, alongside citations for the new datasets, optimizers and FairBatch. The broad research positioning is retained, while 'neither studied, nor understood' is softened to 'largely unexplored.'

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language corrections and expands the NGOS explanation. Fairness-metric definitions move into Section 4, Theorem 3's proof moves to the appendix, appendix sections are reordered, and a NeurIPS checklist is appended. The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables displaying joint tuning, fairness-intervention comparisons and optimizer variants. Existing tables are renumbered and repositioned, and several figures are relocated. All thirteen original figures retain their content and visual design; there is no broad graphical redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central optimizer–fairness relationship. Joint tuning (Table 1), optimizer-variant tests (Appendix N/Table 6), and FairBatch/tabular comparisons (Table 4) address important questions about tuning confounds, the proposed mechanism and applicability beyond v1's vision benchmarks. Reported code access further improves reproducibility, although sparse details for the added protocols limit independent reproduction from the PDFs alone.
